auPontosChave1: • Resistance index measurements from umbilical artery should be taken during fetal apnea and obtained from four different abdominal sites to assure representation of the entire cord length.
auPontosChave2: • Pulsatility index measurement from umbilical artery should be taken with the pulsed Doppler sample volume placed over the cord, in a position considered equidistant from its abdominal and placental insertion points.
auPontosChave3: • The vascular resistance of the fetal arteries decreases linearly during the pregnancy.
auPontosChave4: • A normal umbilical cord contains two arteries and one vein with the vein is larger than the arteries. A single umbilical artery is associated with fetal anomalies.
caPontosChave1: • Among all the biometric measurements routinely performed, the abdominal circumference (AC) has been shown to be more sensitive in detecting growth abnormalities than those measurements based on bone structures.
caPontosMedida1: • A true axial plane through the upper fetal abdomen should be taken.
caPontosMedida2: • The anatomical landmarks that must be visualized at the same view are:
caPontosMedida3: 1. Fetal stomach (s): depicted as an echo-free sac usually at the left side.
caPontosMedida4: 2. Umbilical vein (*): a central echo-free “comma-shaped” structure. Represents the umbilical vein  entering the portal sinus.
caPontosMedida5: 3. Spine: usually depicted as three echogenic ossification centres posteriorly.
caPontosMedida6: • Calliper placement: follows abdominal skin outlining.
ccnLegendaUltra: * When the gestational age < 7 weeks the crown and rump can not be diferentiated; accordingly, the greatest length of the embryo should be measured.
ccnPontosChave1: • The crown-rump length (CRL) is the best parameter for determining gestational age at first-trimester and should be used whenever appropriate.
ccnPontosChave2: • Between the 12th and 14th weeks, crown-rump length and biparietal diameter are similar in accuracy. It is recommended that crown-rump length be used up to 84 mm, and biparietal diameter be used for measurements > 84 mm.
ccnPontosChave3: • When the gestational age based on CRL is within 7 days of that calculated from the LMP, we consider the LMP to be reliable, and take it as the true biological date.
ccnPontosChave4: • Cardiac activity should be present in an embryo with a CRL ≥ 7 mm.
ccnPontosMedidaCorreta1: • Good magnification: the fetus fills almost the entire screen.
ccnPontosMedidaCorreta2: • Mid-sagittal section: the profile, spine and rump are visible.
ccnPontosMedidaCorreta3: • Neutral position: there is fluid visible between the chin and the chest of the fetus (arrow).
ccnPontosMedidaCorreta4: • Fetus is horizontal : 90° to the ultrasound beam.
ccnPontosMedidaCorreta5: • Callipers are placed correctly: the intersection of the calipers should be placed on the outer borders of the skin over the head and rump.
cfPontosChave1: • Femur is the long bone of choice to predict gestational age.
cfPontosChave2: • The transducer should be aligned with the bone long-axis so the beam is perpendicular to the shaft.
cfPontosChave3: • Femoral length is considered accurate when the image shows two blunted ends.
cfPontosChave4: • When the femur shaft is at an angle of over 30 grades to the horizontal plane the measurement may be considered inaccurate.
cfPontosChave5: • Femoral length has an important role in excluding dwarfism in fetus (FL < 2-3 SD’s of the mean).
cfPontosMedida1: • A longitudinal plane through the femur should be taken the closest to 90° with the ultrasound beam.
cfPontosMedida2: • Magnify the image to take a more precise measurement.
cfPontosMedida3: • Length measurement must be taken from blunt end to blunt end parallel to the shaft.
cfPontosMedida4: • Measure the femoral diaphysis and do not include ossification centers.

dbp: Biparietal Diameter and Head Circumference (BPD and HC)
dbpPontosChave1: • Between the 12th and 14th weeks, biparietal diameter (BPD) and crown-rump length (CRL) are similar in accuracy. It is recommended that crown-rump length be used up to 84 mm, and biparietal diameter be used for CRL measurements > 84 mm.
dbpPontosChave2: • Biparietal measurement provide a good estimate of fetal age in the first half of pregnancy (standard deviation of up to 12 days), however, there is a progressive increase in the variability as pregnancy progresses, with a maximum variability of 3.2 weeks in the last six weeks of pregnancy.
dbpPontosChave3: • BPD should not be used for fetal dating when variations in fetal head shape are visualized. In this cases, the cephalic index has been shown an effective way to detect such extremes in fetal head shape.
dbpPontosMedida1: • An axial plane through the fetal head should be taken the closest to 90° with the ultrasound beam.
dbpPontosMedida2: • The anatomical landmarks that must be visualized at the same view are:
dbpPontosMedida3: 1. Septum pellucidum: depicted as two tiny symmetric echogenic lines at one third of the fronto-occipital distance (arrows).
dbpPontosMedida4: 2. Midline falx: a central unique echogenic line (arrowhead).
dbpPontosMedida5: 3. Thalami (t): two symmetrically positioned hypoechoic structures on either side of the falx.
dbpPontosMedida6: • BPD: Measure from outer surface of the skull table in the near field to the inner margin of the skull table in the far field. (outer to inner)
dbpPontosMedida7: • HC: measured at the same plane obtained to BPD. An ellipse may be drawn around the outside of the calvarium.
descricaoPlanoAxial: Plano horizontal que passa transversalmente através do corpo, dividindo as estruturas em partes superior ou cefálica e inferior ou caudal.

descricaoPlanoObliquo: Trata-se de um plano inclinado/angulado sem paralelismo aos demais planos. Desta forma, é um plano complementar aos demais e pode ser considerado auxiliar na descrição de planos inclinados, tais como coronal oblíquo, sagital oblíquo ou axial oblíquo.
descricaoPlanoSagital: Plano vertical que passa longitudinalmente através do corpo, dividindo as estruturas em antímeros direito e esquerdo.

dtcPontosMedida2: • The cerebral peduncules, cerebellar hemispheres and the cisterna magna must be displayed at the same view.
dtcPontosMedida3: • Callipers are kept at the outer margins of the cerebellum at its maximum width.
fcePontosChave1: • Embryonic heart rate (EHR) should be calculated as beats per minute (bpm).
fcePontosChave2: • Measurement is taken by electronic calipers as the distance between two heart waves on a frozen M-mode image.
fcePontosChave3: • Embryonic bradycardia is defined as a heart rate < 100 beats per minute up to 6.2 weeks of gestation (CRL about 4 mm) and < 120 beats per minute at 6.3–7.0 weeks of gestation (CRL about 9 mm).
fcePontosChave4: • Embryonic tachycardia is defined as a heart rate of 135 beats per minute and higher before 6.3 weeks of gestation or 155 beats per minute and higher at 6.3–7.0 weeks of gestation.
fcePontosChave5: • The early increase in HR coincides with the morphological development of the heart, and the subsequent decrease may be the result of functional maturation of the parasympathetic system.
fibulaPontosChave1: • Sonographic measurement of the ossified shafts of fetal long bones is possible after 12 weeks of gestation.
fibulaPontosChave2: • The fibula is located sonographically by sequentially checking the fetal bladder, iliac crest, femoral bone and knee.
fibulaPontosChave3: • Fibula is distinguished from tibia once the fibular plateau is smaller, the fibular diaphysis is thinner than tibial diaphysis and it is the outermost leg bone.
fibulaPontosMedida1: • A coronal plane through the fetal leg should be taken the closest to 90° with the ultrasound beam.
fibulaPontosMedida2: • Magnify the image to take a more precise measurement.
fibulaPontosMedida3: • Length measurement must be taken from blunt end to blunt end parallel to the shaft.
fibulaPontosMedida4: • Fibula is the outermost bone with smaller plateau and thinner shaft.

ilaPontosChave4: • An AFI below the 5th percentile is suggestive of oligohydramnios and above the 95th percentile is suggestive of polyhydramnios.

mensuracao1Pancreas:
Head of the pancreas: located to the right of splenomesenteric confluence and anteriorly to inferior vena cava. 
Pancreatic body: located anteriorly to splenic vein.  The pancreatic tail is visualized best on coronal scans using spleen as a window.
mensuracao1PancreasPediatrico:
Head of the pancreas: located to the right of splenomesenteric confluence.
Pancreatic body: located anteriorly the splenic vein. 
The pancreatic tail can be characterized by transverse section in the upper abdomen, however is visualized best on coronal scans using spleen as a window.
mensuracao2Pancreas: The pancreatic duct should appears either as an anechoic tubular structure (arrowhead) or two parallel echogenic lines (arrow) at the pancreatic body. The diameter of the duct is taken as the distance between the inner layers of the anterior and posterior walls.
mensuracao2PancreasPediatrico: Pancreatic duct can appear either as a single echogenic linear structure or as a tubular structure with smooth, parallel echogenic walls and an anechoic lumen.

modoVisualizacaoTexto:
• Normal: Allows viewing of all the application’s content.  From the basics in ultrasound, passing through preparation and examination technique and finally providing the reference measures. 

• Quick access: Allows quick and objective access to the reference values. The purpose of this type of display is to make measurements and normal values available for those users who already have an expertise in anatomy and ultrasound techniques.

Note:  You can switch between both types of display whenever you want. All you have to do is access  the settings menu and select the desired option in “Quick access only”.
onPontosChave1: • The nasal bone is one of the few facial features that has distinctly identifiable borders and its length can be obtained in a standardized fashion.
onPontosChave2: • Nasal bone measurement should be used as a Down syndrome screening in first trimester.
onPontosChave3: • The ultrasonographic absence of the nasal bone is well stablished as a marker for Down syndrome.
onPontosMedida1: • A mid-sagittal plane of the fetal profile should be taken.
onPontosMedida2: • The fetal nasal bone is identified and measured at the level of the synostosis.

pesoPontosChave1: • In practice the most common equations for calculating the estimated fetal weight (EFW) are based on the standard fetal biometry (BPD,HC,AC and FL).
pesoPontosChave2: • Regardless of the formula used the accuracy of the sonographic estimate of the EFW is affected by suboptimal imaging and biological variation.
pesoPontosChave3: • In addition the accuracy of the sonographic estimate decreases with increasing birth weight, and tends to be overestimated  in pregnancies suspected  of being large for gestational age (LGA) and underestimated  in pregnancies with preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) and suspected fetal growth restriction.
pnPontosChave1: • Nuchal fold is essentially the skin fold behind the fetal occipital region and its thickness should increases with GA.
pnPontosChave2: • Nuchal fold thickening is a specific sonographic marker for aneuploidy in the second-trimester.
pnPontosChave3: • The most  commonly accepted upper limit for nuchal fold thickness is 6 mm up to 20 weeks. However, this threshold still remains valid up to 24 weeks.
pnPontosMedida1: • An axial transcerebellar plane of the fetal head should be taken.
pnPontosMedida2: • The cavum septum pellucidum, atria of lateral ventricles, cerebral peduncles and cerebellar hemispheres must be displayed at the same view.
pnPontosMedida3: • Callipers are placed from the outer edge of the occipital bone to the outer edge of the overlying skin.

tecnica1VBTBPediatrico: Measurement of longitudinal and anteroposterior diameters of the gallbladder should be performed with convex transducer (4-6 Mhz) and/or linear transducers (7-10 MHz) in an extended right intercostal section with the patient in deep inspiration.  Turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise we get the transverse diameter of the gallbladder. The right intercostal window must also be used for its characterization.  The gallbladder wall thickness should be measured in its anterior wall, covering all its visible layers and in a contiguous portion with the liver where the sound beam is directed perpendicular to it. The use of linear transducers can facilitate a better depiction and measurement of its walls.
tecnicaAlcasIntestinaisAdulto: Initially a curvilinear transducer is used (3 - 5 MHZ). Graded compression is applied in order to displace interposing gas and increase conspicuity of abnormal bowel loops. If wall thickening is detected, a detailed evaluation with both gray-scale and color Doppler is performed with a linear or curved high-frequency (7.5 to 12 MHz) transducer.In patients without acute symptoms at least 6 hrs of fasting can be helpful to minimize excessive gas in the intestinal lumen. Harmonic imaging can be useful to increase identification of the bowel layers. Differentiation of small bowel from colon is possible based on location (small bowel is central and large bowel is peripheral), anatomy (valvulae conniventes are present in the small bowel) and peristalsis (usually present in small bowel and absent or minimally present in large bowel).
tecnicaAlcasIntestinaisPediatrico: Initially a curvilinear transducer is used (5 - 7 MHZ). Graded compression is applied in order to displace interposing gas and increase conspicuity of abnormal bowel loops. If wall thickening is detected, a detailed evaluation with both gray-scale and color Doppler is performed with a linear or curved high-frequency (7.5 to 12 MHz) transducer.In patients without acute symptoms at least 4 to 5 hrs of fasting can be helpful to minimize excessive gas in the intestinal lumen. Harmonic imaging can be useful to increase identification of the bowel layers. Differentiation of small bowel from colon is possible based on location (small bowel is central and large bowel is peripheral), anatomy (valvulae conniventes are present in the small bowel) and peristalsis (usually present in small bowel and absent or minimally present in large bowel).
tecnicaAortaIliacas: Use a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) with the patient in the supine position. The use of firm, slow and gradual compression favors the characterization of retroperitoneal vessels, since it displaces intervening intestinal loops. The transducer should be placed in the paramedian sagital plane in the mesogastrium and the anteroposterior diameter of the distal aorta measured immediately before the aortic bifurcation. The common iliac arteries should have their anteroposterior diameters measured immediately after the aortic bifurcation.
tecnicaApendiceAdulto: A linear array transducer (7-12 MHz) is used to gradually compress the right lower quadrant.Gentle gradual pressure is applied to the anterior abdominal wall, resulting in displacement and compression of normal bowel loops. At the start of the examination, the patient is asked to point with a single finger to the site of maximal tenderness or pain.Self-localization expedites the search for an inflamed appendix, especially an aberrantly located appendix, and reduces the time of examination.Scanning begins in the transverse plane with identification of the ascending colon, which appears as a non-peristaltic bowel segment containing gas and fluid. The transducer is then moved inferiorly to identify the cecal tip, where the appendix should arise. Pressure is gradually applied to displace gas and fecal material from the cecum, thus improving visualization of the appendix and distal small bowel. Normal bowel is easily compressible and displays active peristalsis. The psoas muscle and external iliac vessels should be identified, since the appendix lies anteriorly to these structures.
tecnicaBacoAdulto: The spleen must have its longitudinal diameter measured using a convex transducer (2-5 MHz) through a coronal plane at the level of the splenic hilum.  This plane is acquired from an intercostal section obtained through the left lateral intercostal space in a high position, between the middle and posterior axillary line. The exam should be performed in varying degrees of inspiration, in an attempt to maximize the splenic window.  The greatest length between its superomedial margin (splenic dome) and its inferolateral border (spleen tip) should be used at the hilum level.
tecnicaBacoPediatrico: The spleen must have its longitudinal diameter measured using a convex or sectorial transducer (2-5 MHz for older children; 4-7 MHz for younger children) through a coronal plane at the level of the splenic hilum. The measurement of the splenic length is made from its most superomedial point (splenic dome) to the most inferolateral one (spleen tip).
tecnicaBexigaAdulto:
Use a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) for characterization of the bladder, which should be moderately distended, because with exaggerated distension the examination becomes uncomfortable for the patient. The postvoid residual volume is made by measuring the largest transverse axis in the axial plane and the longitudinal and anteroposterior axes in the sagital plane. The calculation of the bladder volume obeys the formula:  L x AP x T x 0.52. 
Measurements of the bladder wall thickness should preferably be made on the anterior wall. You can magnify using the “zoom” control on the image obtained with a convex transducer or using a linear transducer (7.5 Mhz) for a better characterization of the wall. Wall measurement should be made by measuring the thickness of the detrusor muscle, seen as a hypoechogenic layer between the internal hyperechogenic mucosal layer and the external hyperechogenic serous layer.
tecnicaBexigaPediatrico: The bladder volume index (BVI) is calculated with a convex transducer first by measuring the maximum length (L) of the urinary bladder on the longitudinal scan, which is obtained from the neck to the fundus of bladder. Then the transducer is rotated 90o counterclockwise and the bladder scanned from superiorly to inferiorly to locate the maximum transverse section. Depth (D) is measured in the midline from anterior to posterior mucosal surface of the bladder. The width (W) is taken perpendicular to D at its mid-point. BVI is calculated from the formula: L x D x W (in centimeters). Bladder wall thickness is measured when the residual volume  is < 10% of the original because its measurement is difficult and least accurate when the bladder is full. Measurement is taken from a zoomed image of the transverse plane of the voided bladder at three points:anterolaterally, laterally and posterolaterally, the the mean is taken from these three measurements. The final index, BVWI, is calculated by the above data from the formula: Maximum BVI / average wall thickness.
tecnicaEndometrioAdulto: Endometrial thickness is taken in the sagittal plane of the uterus at the thickest part near the fundus, including both endometrial layers, excluding any intracavitary fluid.
tecnicaEpididimosAdulto: The epididymis should be examined with a high frequency linear transducer (7-15 MHz). The patient should be placed in the supine position and may be asked to hold the penis in a position of anteriorization of the penis belly, leading it towards the navel, and placing a towel beneath the scrotum to provide support and facilitate the exposure of the epididymis. The epididymal head is a pyramid-shaped structure situated on the upper pole  of the testis. It is homogeneous and almost isoechoic compared with the testis. The epididymal body is contiguous to the head and is situated on the posterior-lateral aspect of the testis and is less echogenic than the head.
tecnicaFigadoAdulto: The measurements of the longitudinal diameter of the left lobe (LL) and right lobe (RL) of the liver should be performed using a convex transducer (2-5Mhz) in mid-sternal and midclavicular line, respectively.  Performing a deep inspiration as well as a cranial angulation of the transducer allows the characterization of the liver diaphragmatic surface, indispensable for its measurement.
tecnicaFigadoPediatrico: The measurement of the longitudinal diameter of the right lobe should be performed using a convex transducer (3-5 MHz) in the right midclavicular line.  Measurement should be done from the most cranial point of the diaphragmatic surface of liver to its lower border.
tecnicaOvariosAdulto: Use a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) for a suprapubic approach and an endocavitary transducer for a transvaginal sonography. The ovaries should be  characterized in adnexal regions bilaterally. In a parasagittal plane, measure the largest longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (AP) ovarian axis. By turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise, the largest transverse axis (T) is measured. Calculation of ovarian volume obeys the formula: L x AP x T x 0.52.
tecnicaOvariosPediatrico: Choose a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) with the patient in the supine position, using the full bladder as an acoustic window. Serial longitudinal scans of the pelvis with the uterus as a landmark should be made by tilting the transducer and scanning through the bladder from the contralateral side. The ovaries are characterized as hypoechoic oval structures in relation to the adjacent tissues, about halfway from the uterus to the iliopsoas muscle. The ovarian vessels can also be used as additional landmarks.  The largest longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (A) ovarian axis are measured. By turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise, the transverse axis (T) is measured. Formula for calculating the ovarian volume: L x Ap x T x 0.52.
tecnicaPancreasAdulto: The head and pancreatic body are characterized with a convex transducer (2-5 Mhz) in a  transverse section of the upper abdomen, being able to use the left lobe of the liver or the fluid-filled stomach as an acoustic window for its characterization. The measurement of the pancreatic head (located laterally to the right of the portomesenteric confluence and anteriorly to inferior vena cava) is made by calculating its anteroposterior diameter. The pancreatic body should be measured in its middle portion, anterior to the splenic vein. The main pancreatic duct is well depicted and should be measured in its body portion. The pancreatic tail is hardly seen in this anterior approach and the spleen should be used as an acoustic window for its characterization.
tecnicaPancreasPediatrico: Pancreatic head and body measurements should be performed with a sector or convex transducer (5-7.5 MHz). The largest diameters of the head and body should be measured through a transverse section of the upper abdomen with the patient in supine position using the left lobe of the liver as an acoustic window. The pancreatic tail is visualized best on coronal scans using spleen as a window.
tecnicaParatireoideAdulto: Images are obtained in the longitudinal and transverse planes with a high frequency linear probe (7-12MHz). The patient should be placed in the supine position and with cervical hyperextension by placing cushion or pillow at the level of the shoulder girdle facilitating the fall of the head backwards. Commonly parathyroid glands are not seen at a routine neck ultrasound. Occasionally, the normal parathyroid gland can be identified separate from thyroid tissue, especially in a longitudinal view. The normal parathyroid gland may either be seen as a slightly low reflective oval area posterior to the normal thyroid.
tecnicaPiloroPediatrico: In the supine position with a linear transducer in a transverse position and sometimes with slight anti-clockwise rotation, identify the gallbladder. The pylorus is usually located slightly medial and posterior in relation to the gallbladder.
tecnicaProstata: Use a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) for a suprapubic approach to the prostate. Using the bladder as the acoustic window, the characterization of the prostate should be done in the sagittal and axial planes with a slight caudal angulation of the transducer. Perform the measurement of the transverse axis (T) prostate in the axial plane, and the longitudinal axis (L) and anteroposterior (AP) in the sagittal plane.  The calculation of the prostate volume obeys the formula:  L x AP x T x 0.52. For the calculation of intravesical prostatic protrusion (IPP), measure the vertical distance from the tip of the protrusion to the base of bladder.
tecnicaRimAdulto: The kidneys should be evaluated in the transverse and longitudinal planes and through two main sections: subcostal and intercostal in the flanks. The patient should be placed in the supine, left or right oblique position. The visualization of the kidney through the subcostal section should be made in deep inspiration, being measured through the coronal plane its greater longitudinal diameter. The intercostal section is useful in characterizing the kidneys as well as the echogenicity compared to the spleen and liver.  Measurement of renal parenchymal thickness should be performed preferably in the middle third from the outer renal cortical margin to the outer margin of the sinus echoes.
tecnicaRimPediatrico: The kidneys must be evaluated with sector (3.5-7.5 MHz) or convex (4-6.0 MHz) transducer.  The visualization of the kidney is made through the subcostal section in the flanks, being measured through the coronal plane its greater longitudinal diameter.
tecnicaSuprarrenalPediatrico: Adrenal glands examination should be performed using a sector or linear transducer (7 - 12 Mhz). Its identification is routinely done scanning from the flanks in sagittal an coronal projections. Echogenicity, homogeneity and size of both glands must be evaluated. Normal adrenal gland is identified in a suprarenal location and have an inverted Y-shape in the longitudinal plane.
tecnicaTesticulosAdulto: The testicles should be examined with a high frequency linear transducer (7-15 MHz).  Using lower frequency transducers (3-5 MHz) may be necessary in patients with marked hydrocele or testicular mass. The patient should be placed in the supine position and may be asked to hold the penis in a position of anteriorization of the penis belly, leading it towards the navel, and placing a towel beneath the scrotum to provide support and facilitate the exposure of the testes and satisfactory testicular measurement. The scrotal volume is given by the formula:  0.52 x L x T x Ap, where: L - longitudinal diameter of the scrotum measured in its sagittal axis, Ap - anteroposterior diameter and T - transverse diameter, both measured in an axial section of the testicles.
tecnicaTesticulosPediatrico: The testicles should be examined with a high frequency linear transducer (7-15 MHz).  Using lower frequency transducers (3-5 MHz) may be necessary in patients with marked hydrocele. The patient should be placed in the supine position. Should be necessary a towel beneath the scrotum to provide support and facilitate the exposure of the testes and satisfactory testicular measurement. The scrotal volume is given by the formula:  0.52 x L x T x Ap, where: L - longitudinal diameter of the scrotum measured in its sagittal axis, Ap - anteroposterior diameter and T - transverse diameter, both measured in an axial section of the testicles.
tecnicaTireoideAdulto: The thyroid should be examined with a high frequency linear transducer (7-15 MHz).  The use of lower frequency convex transducers (3-5Mhz) may be required for proper measurement of the gland in obese patients or patients with goiter. The patient should be placed in the supine position and with cervical hyperextension by placing a cushion or a pillow at the level of the shoulder girdle facilitating the fall of the head backwards.  The measurement of the gland volume is through obtaining measures of its largest longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (AP) axis, performed in a sagittal section of the lobes, and its transverse diameter (T), obtained in an axial section of the lobes.  The estimated volume of each lobe is given by the formula:  L x AP x T x 0.52. The total volume of the gland will be given by the sum of both lobes and the isthmus, which interferes little in the final volume of the thyroid.
tecnicaTireoidePediatrico: The thyroid should be examined with a high frequency linear transducer (7-15 MHz). The patient should be placed in the supine position and with cervical hyperextension by placing a cushion or a pillow at the level of the shoulder girdle facilitating the fall of the head backwards.  The measurement of the gland volume is through obtaining measures of its largest longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (AP) axis, performed in a sagittal section of the lobes, and its transverse diameter (T), obtained in an axial section of the lobes.  The estimated volume of each lobe is given by the formula:  L x AP x T x 0.52. The total volume of the gland will be given by the sum of both lobes and the isthmus, which interferes little in the final volume of the thyroid.
tecnicaToraxAdulto: Sonography should be performed with the patient supine and during maximum inspiration. With the intercostal space used as acoustic window, the transducer was applied at the laterodorsal part of the chest wall. A position just cranial to the base of the lung was sought, and a strictly transverse scan was obtained. From this image, the maximum perpendicular distance  between the posterior surface of the lung and the posterior chest wall was measured.
tecnicaTransfontanelaPediatrico: Scans should be performed with a convex or sectorial probe (5-8 Mhz). Usually scanning is performed at the bedside with the infant’s head in supine position. With the anterior fontanel used as an acoustic window, standard views are obtained in the coronal and sagittal planes.
tecnicaTratoAdulto: CBD is imaged from an extended intercostal section in the longitudinal plane or from an intercostal section with the patient in supine or right anterior oblique position. The common duct is measured at the point that passes anterior to the right portal vein, often with the hepatic artery seen in cross section between the duct and the vein. Measurements are taken from inner wall to inner wall and should be perpendicular to the course of the duct.
tecnicaTratoPediatrico: The common duct (CD) is imaged from an extended intercostal section in the longitudinal plane or from an intercostal section with the patient in supine or right anterior oblique position. The common duct is measured at the point that passes anterior to the right portal vein, often with the hepatic artery seen in cross section between the duct and the vein. Measurements are taken from inner wall to inner wall and should be perpendicular to the course of the duct.
tecnicaUteroAdulto:
Use the convex transducer (3-5Mhz) with patient in supine position and full bladder for transabdominal scan. Using the bladder as acoustic window, evaluate the maximum longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (AP) diameter of the uterus in a sagittal section plane. By turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise the largest transverse diameter of the uterine body should be measured. 
Through a transvaginal approach, using an endocavitary transducer, the largest longitudinal (L) and anteroposterior (AP) axis of the uterus should be characterized in a sagittal plane. By turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise the largest transverse diameter of the uterine body is measured. The calculation of the uterine volume obeys the prolate ellipsoid formula:  L x AP x T x 0.52.
tecnicaUteroPediatrico: Use a convex transducer (3-5Mhz) with the patient in the supine position. Evaluate the total uterine length (TUL)  in a suprapubic midsagittal plane.  In the same plane, the anteroposterior diameter of the corpus (COAP) and the cervix (CEAP) are measured. By turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise the widest transverse diameter of the corpus is measured.
tecnicaVBAdulto: Measurement of longitudinal diameter of the gallbladder should be performed with convex transducer (2-5 Mhz) in an extended right intercostal section with the patient in deep inspiration.  Turning the transducer 90 degrees counterclockwise we get the transverse diameter of the gallbladder. The right intercostal window must also be used for its characterization.  The gallbladder wall thickness should be measured in its anterior wall, covering all its visible layers and in a contiguous portion with the liver where the sound beam is directed perpendicular to it. The use of linear transducers can facilitate a better depiction and measurement of its walls
tecnicaVCIAdulto: Use a convex transducer (3 – 5 Mhz) with the patient in the supine position. IVC characterization is done by placing the transducer in the transverse plane in the epigastrium measuring the long and short axis of IVC approximately 1 cm below the level of the left renal vein. On the other hand, hepatic veins are depicted at a right subcostal scanning, moving the probe toward the patient right shoulder in attempt to see the hepatic veins confluence. Measurement of hepatic veins must be taken 2 cm far from their confluence with IVC.
tecnicaVaricoceleAdulto: The pampiniform venous plexus must be evaluated with a high frequency linear transducer (7-12 MHz). Patient should be examined in supine and standing position. Measurements of pampiniform venous plexus diameters’ must be taken at B mode. Doppler mode is also important to evaluate under basal (resting) conditions and during the Valsalva maneuver to evaluate venous reflux.
tecnicaVeiaPortaAdulto: Using a convex transducer (3-5 Mhz), scan through a right extended intercostal section with the patient in deep inspiration to characterize its greatest anteroposterior diameter in the hepatic hilum. The right intercostal section is also useful in the characterization of the portal vein, especially for a Doppler study, because in this section the vein appears more upright, making it easier to obtain the correct angles for measuring its velocity.
tecnicaVeiaPortaPediatrico: A curved linear transducer (5-7.5 Mhz) should be used in infants and small childrens. In larger patients, a 3-5 MHz may be needed. Using an extended intercostal or an intercostal section, with the child in spontaneous breathing, locate the portal vein in the region of the hepatic hilum and perform the measurement of its largest anteroposterior diameter.

tibiaPontosChave1: • Sonographic measurement of the ossified shafts of fetal long bones is possible after 12 weeks of gestation.
tibiaPontosChave2: • The tibia is located sonographically by sequentially checking the fetal bladder, iliac crest, femoral bone and knee.
tibiaPontosChave3: • Tibia is distinguished from fibula once the tibial plateau is larger, the tibial diaphysis is thicker than fibula diaphysis and it is the innermost leg bone.
tibiaPontosMedida1: • A coronal plane through the fetal leg should be taken the closest to 90° with the ultrasound beam.
tibiaPontosMedida2: • Magnify the image to take a more precise measurement.
tibiaPontosMedida3: • Length measurement must be taken from blunt end to blunt end parallel to the shaft.
tibiaPontosMedida4: • Tibia is the innermost bone with larger plateau and thicker shaft.
tnPontosChave1: • The optimal gestational age for measurement of fetal NT is 11 weeks to 13 weeks and 6 days.
tnPontosChave2: • The minimum fetal crown–rump length should be 45 mm and the maximum 84 mm.
tnPontosMedida2: • A mid-sagittal section of the fetus should be obtained and the NT should be measured with the fetus in the neutral position.
tnPontosMedida3: • Only the fetal head and upper thorax should be included in the image. The magnification should be as large as possible and always such that each slight movement of the callipers produces only a 0.1 mm change in the measurement.
tnPontosMedida4: • The maximum thickness of the subcutaneous translucency between the skin and the soft tissue overlying the cervical spine should be measured. Care must be taken to distinguish between fetal skin and amnion.
tnPontosMedida5: • The callipers should be placed on the lines that define the NT thickness – the crossbar of the calliper should be such that it is hardly visible as it merges with the white line of the border and not in the nuchal fluid.
tnPontosMedida6: • During the scan, more than one measurement must be taken and the maximum one should be recorded.
ulnaPontosMedida1: • After visualizing the humerus, the transducer is moved following its  shaft toward the elbow. Rotation of the probe around the elbow demonstrates the ulna and radius. The ulna is distinguished from radius because the ulnar shaft penetrates much deeper into the elbow than the radius.
umeroPontosChave1: • Sonographic measurement of the ossified shaft of fetal humerus is possible after the 12th week of gestation.
umeroPontosChave2: • HL is a useful parameter for assessing GA in conjunction with FL, when other parameters do not accurately predict GA.
umeroPontosMedida1: • After visualizing the heart, the transducer is moved to image the scapular spine which is dorsal to the humerus head. The full length of the humerus is then obtained in a plane as close as possible to right angles of the ultrasound beam. A straight measurement should be made from the center of one end of the diaphysis to the other, disregarding any curvature.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave1: • YS is the first extraembryonic structure detected with transvaginal sonography.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave2: • Its visualization is diagnostic of an intrauterine pregnancy.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave3: • It can be seen from the 4.5th to the 12th gestational week.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave4: • Appears as a spherical translucent structure with echogenic walls within the gestational sac.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave5: • YS diameter must be taken from the distance between its inner walls.
vesiculaVitelinicaPontosChave6: • As a general rule the  normal YS diameter is up to 6 mm.
vlPontosMedida1: • A transventricular axial plane of the fetal head should be obtained.
vlPontosMedida2: • Midline structures must be equidistant from the calvarial margins.
vlPontosMedida3: • Measurement is taken as the transverse diameter of the atrium.  The glomus of the choroid plexus is used to locate the atrium.
vlPontosMedida4: • Calipers are placed on the inner to inner margins of the ventricular wall at its widest part.
